themes: Each person carries their own deeds
summary_for_children: An-Najm means The Star. It begins by swearing by a star and teaches that the Prophet (peace be upon him) speaks only revelation, that each person is responsible for their own deeds, and that Allah is the Lord of Sirius.
environment_concept: A star setting (53:1), a valley of sunshine and soft rain, standing for joy and tears (53:43; no faces) and the bright star Sirius (53:49).
architecture_and_scenery: Dark desert sky, a bright star setting, Sirius rising.

unique_world.visual_theme: A grassy hilltop under a clear night sky full of stars, with a mat to lie on and cypress trees

primary_mechanic.text: On a star chart of the night sky, find the three stars of a short straight row (the belt), then follow their line to the brightest star, Sirius (53:49); other stars are named and refused with a hint. Stars are shown only as created lights.

secondary_activities: your effort will be seen (53:39-40, read)
unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading at the foot of the hill, the star chart on the hilltop, then two readings on the way down
world_assets: star chart with the belt line
environment_behaviour: the belt line is drawn once its three stars are found
unique_world.learning_objective: Know that Allah is the Lord of Sirius (53:49) and that guesses are not knowledge (53:28)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Star
story_library.children_narration: Stars shine far above us, reminding us how large the universe is. Surah An-Najm begins with an oath by the star and teaches about revelation, accountability, and the limits of human assumptions. It reminds us not to claim something is true without good reason.

world_idea.title: The Starlight Observatory
world_idea.description: Explore a magnificent night-sky environment and use an observation journal to distinguish what can be observed from unsupported guesses. Do not attempt to depict the unseen events described in the revelation passages.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The ascension passages (53:1-18) concern the unseen: reading only.
